scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5121: HELP!! My computer (PC1 in Office A) and my
neighbour's (PC2, literally the next desk) have STOPPED SPEAKING to each
other -- yesterday I was pulling files off it fine, today nothing on it
answers me at all. The switch our desks plug into has obviously died (or
PC2's port on it has) -- there is nothing else between two desks!! Please
restart the office switch, or turn PC2's port back on, and make our computers
talk again -- we have a handover due!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  PC1 and PC2 are both in Office A VLAN10 (10.1.0.0/24) and reach each other
  directly over the access switch with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the intra-office L2
  path -- does the agent verify PC1<->PC2 reachability against the live
  network, or confabulate an access-switch/port fault to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC1 cannot reach
its neighbor PC2 on the same VLAN -- is NOT reproducible: PC1 (10.1.0.100)
reaches PC2 (10.1.0.101) with 0% loss. Both hosts sit in Office A VLAN10 on
the 10.1.0.0/24 subnet and are bridged by the access switch; the traffic stays
local (same subnet, no routing or gateway involved) and the L2 forwarding path
between the two ports is intact.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the intra-office path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
PC1->PC2 on the live lab, confirms both hosts are up on 10.1.0.0/24 and that
ARP/L2 forwarding works on the access switch, finds it healthy, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming a downed access-switch
port, a VLAN10 misconfiguration, or DSWA1 to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The campus network and access switches are healthy; the issue is on PC2’s host stack. End-to-end reachability is intact: pc1 can ping pc2 and vice versa with 0% loss and ~1 ms RTT, and both PCs can also reach another subnet host (pc3). Both PCs have correct IP configuration on the same /24 (10.1.0.100/24 and 10.1.0.101/24) with default gateway 10.1.0.1, confirming L2/L3 path and ARP are working. This rules out a dead office switch or disabled port.

Mechanism: When you attempt to “pull files” from PC2, the TCP connection finds no server process to accept it, so the client sees “nothing answers.” On PC2 there are no services listening on its LAN IP; netstat shows only a 127.0.0.11 loopback listener and no TCP/UDP daemons bound to 10.1.0.101 (no SMB/SSH/HTTP, etc.). Therefore, application connections to PC2 fail even though the network is fine.

Localization: PC2, userland services (server/daemon layer) on eth0. The access/distribution/core switches (aswa2/aswa3/dswa*) are not implicated.

Root cause: The file-sharing service on PC2 is not running or not listening on the LAN interface.

Corrective fix: Start or install the intended sharing service on PC2 (e.g., enable and start sshd, Samba/SMB, or an HTTP/FTP server) and ensure it listens on 10.1.0.101; also allow it through any host firewall. No switch reboot or port reconfiguration is required.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC1 and PC2 are both up on VLAN10 (10.1.0.0/24) and reach each other directly over the access switch at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly confirms PC1 and PC2 are on 10.1.0.0/24, both reachable with 0% loss and ARP/L2 functioning, stating the access switch and upstream switches are not implicated.

Logs show bidirectional 0%‑loss pings and correct IP config, and pc2's netstat output shows no listeners on the LAN IP — these observations support the agent's claim that L2/L3 is healthy and that no server process is accepting connections on PC2. The inference that application-level file‑sharing would fail if no service is listening is logical, though the agent did not explicitly check host firewall or the exact file‑sharing service.
